items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: The famous two. Me, Badlacks, Lewis Givens, Poire. Went there two nights a week. See, them boys was playing there, you know.

ctx.x: Was it a nickel a dance or a dime or what? Yeah, nickel a dance, three dances a dime I think. Ten cents or three for a quarter. Yeah. I don't know whether he played any white dances or not, but I know he played quite a few.

Yeah. the taxi dances. That's Chitney, huh? That's Chitney dance. Is it Nicola dance or dime? Yeah, Nicola dance. Three dances of dime, I think. Ten cents or three for a quarter, something like that. I wake there and meet Handy. Handy, Lewis Givens, Raymond Brown, something, senior, and junior, and Sidney Flusia. Lewis Givens died when he was pretty young, didn't he? Yeah, Lewis lived too fast. Smoking,

weeds, drinking, lost his health. He and Sales used to be together. That's when I first met Sales. Yeah, with Lewis. Yeah, they were playing someplace on the riverside of Bourbon, I can't remember. Bourbon Street? Yeah, and they used to play Purple Rose of Cairo and all the things that they did. They Piron things for me, all the pretty Piron things. Oh, back to the Levita, was it a good-paying job? 25 a week. I guess that's good.
